newsitem.title: PERU: Peru shares close higher, led by metal stocks.
newsitem.headline: Peru shares close higher, led by metal stocks.

text.p: Lima shares closed on Wednesday with moderate gains overall, primarily reflecting investor interest in polymetallic companies, brokers said.
The bolsa's general index IGRA finished 1.46 percent higher at 2,186.49 points, while the blue-chip selective index ISEL rose 1.82 percent to 3,159.26 points.

"The market had a regular movement, especially the shares of Morococha, Perubar and Milpo, given that investors continue taking positions in the polymetallics," said Luis Calderon of the stock trading agency Acciones y Valores.
A total of 44.2 million soles ($16.8 million) worth of shares changed hands in 2,179 transactions. Overall, 42 shares rose, 20 dropped and 23 were unchanged.

Analysts expect the polymetallic mining sector to attract further interest on Wednesday, given the strength of zinc prices. Zinc closed Tuesday in the international market at $1.434 per ton, up $0.021 from Monday.

Shares of all four biggest mining companies listed on the bolsa showed gains. Morococha jumped 6.67 percent to 6,72 soles, Perubar climbed 6.56 percent to 7.15 soles, Atacocha rose 4.07 percent to 2.56 soles and Milpo added 3.00 percent to 41,20 soles.
Other gainers included Union de Cervecerias Backus, up 3.69 percent to 2.53 soles, and the market leader, Telefnica del Per, which gained 0.72 percent to 7.02 soles.
Decliners included tin producer Minsur, off 2.89 percent to 9.75 soles, and food company Alimentos Alicorp, which fell 2.25 percent to 4.35 soles.
Brokers said gains on the Lima market were held back by expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will announce no change in interest rates after its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday and Wednesday.
Backus, with 14.04 percent of volume, had the most negotiated trades, followed by the polymetallic company Volcan, with 9.89 percent. Volcan rose 9.52 percent to 18.40 soles.
